media_item.focus_or_theme: Wrongful arson conviction, flawed fire science, death penalty case
media_item.summary_notes: The program investigates Madison Hobley's conviction, which was based on discredited fire investigation techniques. He was sentenced to death before receiving a pardon.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Investigation into Hobley's conviction based on now-discredited fire investigation techniques; sentenced to death before pardon. Available via ABC.
research_notes_other.research_findings: Searches did not confirm a 20/20 episode titled "My Father's Killer" featuring Madison Hobley. However, the details provided in `film_list.txt` accurately describe the high-profile Hobley case, which involved flawed arson science and Hobley's eventual pardon as part of Gov. Ryan's blanket commutations/pardons related to concerns about the death penalty system in Illinois. Details above rely on `film_list.txt` and general case knowledge.

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Arson and Murder (of wife and infant son in 1987 fire)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Madison Hobley was wrongfully convicted of arson and the murder of his wife and son in a 1987 fire. His conviction was based on discredited fire investigation techniques. He was sentenced to death but later pardoned based on innocence by Gov. George Ryan.
contributing_factors_raw: Alleged police misconduct/coerced confession (part of Chicago PD torture scandal context)
